wave: open the continuation read contract to a representation-neutral logical view
frozen: 2026-09-26, against main cf9c5309 (CONTINUATION-MEM-1 merged #549 and closed #551; CONTINUATION-PLUGIN-1 closed #550)
status: FORECAST — frozen before implementation; the execution record goes in continuation-view-1-notes.json and this file is not edited
question: Can the executor consume continuation state through a representation-neutral view such that providers may expose row-backed, contiguous and windowed storage without duplication, per-row allocation, or retention of unreachable rows, while preserving exact execution?
why: CONTINUATION-MEM-1 measured three costs forced by the read contract `keys(layer) -> &[Vec<f32>]` from position 0 (class a): canonical/v1's mirror of every K/V row (313 MB on gemma3-4b at 1,124 positions, 1× payload, and canonical/v1 is the server's provider); rows below a sliding window that no provider may drop (24 MB there, ≈1.7 GB at 8,192); and one heap allocation per row. The inventory (`docs/continuation-view-1-inventory.md`) shows the dependency is shallow: kernels already read rows one at a time through `Fn(usize) -> &[f32]`; six index expressions and ConvQkv's two accessors are the whole indexing surface. VIEW-1 is scoped from those class (a) findings only.

retention_authority.rule: The execution plan declares the earliest logical position that can still be requested. A provider must retain everything from there onward, and is never required to retain anything earlier.
retention_authority.shape: ONE plan-owned operation per layer — `required_range(position) -> Range<usize>` (or `required_history_start(position)`) on LayerKvGeometry or the nearest plan-owned type. Global attention and ConvQkv answer start 0; sliding attention answers the window floor.
retention_authority.consumers: reference, production and device execution all obtain their source range from it; none recomputes the sliding floor. A provider may retain a superset.
retention_authority.not: providers interpreting `window` themselves; `window` stays a geometry fact, not a retention permission

view.shape: a logical position range over a backing the executor does not see: `base()`, `end()`, `key(p)`, `value(p) -> &[f32]` for ABSOLUTE positions p, with a typed, named refusal for p outside [base, end).
view.general_not_windowed: the view names no retention policy. row/v1 and a contiguous store answer base = 0; a retaining provider advances base. Nothing in the type says 'sliding window'.
view.checked_before_kernels: before a step executes, the plan's required range for that layer is checked against the view's [base, end); a provider that dropped a required row is refused by name — never an index panic
view.constraints: no allocation per `keys`/`values`-equivalent call; the concrete representation (trait object, enum or generic) is chosen in V2 and recorded in the notes before code, with its dispatch cost measured
invariants: end == the number of logical rows ever appended for that layer (end is logical, never a physical row count)
key(p) / value(p) succeed only for base <= p < end; any other p is the named refusal

A_contiguous_authority.claim: canonical/v1 serves the view directly from its matrix; the mirrored Vec<Vec<f32>> is gone
A_contiguous_authority.proof: STRUCTURAL, and the only thing A is adjudicated on: (1) zero mirrored Vec<Vec<f32>> allocations in canonical/v1 (per-append duplicate allocations = 0 on the MEM-1 harness, was exactly 2); (2) no K/V representation in canonical/v1 attributable to the old read contract (its K/V backings are the matrices alone); (3) logits bit-identical to row/v1
A_contiguous_authority.falsified_if: any mirror or per-row allocation remains, a second K/V representation remains, or one logit bit differs
A_contiguous_authority.magnitude_forecast_secondary: reported, NOT adjudicated as pass/fail for A: canonical K/V allocated = matrix capacity only, so canonical/row ∈ [1.0, 2.0] (was [2.0, 3.0]); gemma3-4b at 1,124 positions ≈883 MB → ≈570 MB. Allocator and growth-step details may move these; a miss is recorded as a magnitude deviation, not a failure of A.

B_retained_range_authority.claim: a provider that retains exactly the plan's required range physically frees every row below it, and execution is unchanged
B_retained_range_authority.provider: an EXACT-retention TEST provider in a test target (not WINDOW-1's shipped provider): after each append it advances base to the plan's required floor and drops the rows below
B_retained_range_authority.forecast: after EVERY append, for every layer: base == required_range(position).start and end == position + 1; base is monotonically non-decreasing; the rows below base are deallocated (live-allocation table, MEM-1 harness); logits bit-identical to row/v1 on the sliding fixture and on gemma3-4b past its window; resident rows per sliding layer = the required range's length, not n; a seeded variant that drops ONE required row is refused by name before the kernel runs
B_retained_range_authority.falsified_if: any append leaves base or end off those values, base ever decreases, a row below base is still allocated, a logit bit differs, or the seeded drop reaches a kernel or panics

C_simple_provider_unchanged.claim: row/v1 migrates to the view and stays the cheap path
C_simple_provider_unchanged.forecast: bit-identical to its MEM-1 baseline logits on every MEM-1 subject; still 0 row-sized allocations and adoption of the moved-in row on every append; 0 allocations inside the view's read calls
C_simple_provider_unchanged.falsified_if: a logit bit differs, or row/v1 gains any allocation or copy

structural_falsifiers.claim: no production absolute indexing into provider rows outside the view implementation
structural_falsifiers.witness: source scan: no `step.keys[` / `step.values[` (baseline 6) and no index into a provider row slice outside the view

no reference, production or device backend computes a retention or source floor from `window` independently of the plan-owned required_range. Judged on authority, not source text: mechanical reuse or inlining of the plan's own helper is fine.
structural_falsifiers.falsified_if: a backend derives a floor from `window` (or any other geometry) itself (baseline: production `source_start`, reused by device, and a reference duplicate)

structural_falsifiers.claim: a retention bug is a refusal, not a panic
structural_falsifiers.witness: seeded provider whose base exceeds the required start → the named refusal, on every backend
structural_falsifiers.falsified_if: an index panic, or a silent read

structural_falsifiers.claim: the plugin boundary moves with the contract, and the new boundary is usable
structural_falsifiers.witness: (1) the ABI stamp is revised with the trait change (larql-plugin/2 → /3); (2) a /2 plugin is refused with the named revision mismatch; (3) the /3 C6 fixture loads through the real loader; (4) the C5 external journey passes in process; (5) the C6 CLI journey passes through the dylib — all bit-identical to canonical/v1 as before
structural_falsifiers.falsified_if: the trait changes under an unchanged stamp, /2 is not refused by name, or /3 cannot load or regresses C5/C6

explicit_questions_not_acceptance.question: Does the view let ConvQkv borrow its K/V rows beside `&mut` recurrent state (a split borrow over disjoint provider storage), removing MEM-1's 2·h-row copy per call?
explicit_questions_not_acceptance.rule: NOT a success criterion. VIEW-1 must not introduce a lifetime or API shape that PRECLUDES a later split borrow. Re-measured with the MEM-1 harness on oute AFTER V2 (the borrow structure is set there) and again after V3. If the 2·h copy remains, that is clean evidence it is an operator issue, not a view-contract one, and ConvQkv gets its own perf rung.

explicit_questions_not_acceptance.question: Should MLA's LatentKvRows (the same from-0 pattern) adopt the view?
explicit_questions_not_acceptance.rule: permitted, not required: MEM-1 measured no class (a) cost there (allocated = payload)

limits_stated: Row-backed, contiguous, retained-range and paged backings fit [base, end) with absolute access.

Remote continuation is compatible only through materialised or cache-backed rows: `key(p) -> &[f32]` needs the bytes local for the borrow. Direct remote fetch may need a different access model; VIEW-1 does not claim it.
